content.productDescription:
Gracing your home with this artwork for a living room feels genuinely special — and I think that is exactly the right word for this piece. At its heart sits beautifully rendered Arabic calligraphy spelling out the Ayat an-Nur, meaning 'Allah is the Light of the Heavens and the Earth', rendered in rich rose gold and deep brown tones. Swirling around it are fluid, marbled waves of dusty blue, soft blush, and warm taupe on a clean white background — giving the whole composition a sense of gentle, flowing movement. It is bold without being loud, and meaningful without needing to explain itself.

What I really love about this print is how the abstract marbling carries both warmth and calm at the same time. The rose gold tones in the calligraphy catch the eye first, and then you notice how the blue and blush waves draw you deeper into the design. It works beautifully as a single statement piece — the kind of art that people actually stop and look at. Whether you are decorating for Ramadan, gifting for Eid, or simply want Islamic art that feels contemporary and personal, this one genuinely delivers.

How to Style Artwork for a Living Room with Islamic Calligraphy

I would position this print as a true focal point — perhaps centred above a sofa or mantelpiece, where the marbled swirls and calligraphy can really breathe. Because the artwork combines deep blues, warm blush, and rose gold, it sits naturally alongside neutral walls in warm white, soft grey, or even a muted sage green. If your living room leans more maximalist, the clean white background keeps it from competing with patterned soft furnishings — it holds its own without overwhelming the space.

For a cohesive Islamic-inspired interior, you might consider pairing this print with geometric cushions or a woven prayer-mat-style rug in complementary blue and blush tones. A single warm-toned light source nearby — a brass lamp, for instance — will pick out the rose gold in the calligraphy beautifully come evening. If you would like to explore more Islamic and calligraphy art prints that work in this way, have a browse through our Islamic wall art collection for pieces that complement this style perfectly.

Choosing the Right Size and Tone for Your Space

When it comes to picking the right version of this print, the first thing I always suggest is measuring the wall space before you order. This is a single statement piece, so it deserves room — going a size larger than you think you need often works better than playing it safe. If the wall is wide, a larger format lets the marbled detail and calligraphy really show themselves off.

In terms of colour, the rose gold calligraphy is the star here, so think about what else is already in the room. Warm metallics, natural wood tones, and soft blue or blush accents will all sing alongside it. If your current palette is quite cool and grey, this print will actually add a lovely warmth that softens the space rather than clashing. And if you are buying it as a gift — for Eid, Ramadan, a new home, or simply to show someone you care — the combination of a meaningful Quranic verse and genuinely contemporary design makes it a gift that will be treasured rather than tucked away.

aiItems.content:
What is artwork for a living room?

Artwork for a living room is any wall art print or decorative piece chosen specifically to enhance the main shared space of a home — adding personality, colour, and meaning to the walls. It can range from abstract prints and photography to calligraphy and Islamic art, depending on your personal style and the atmosphere you want to create. The best living room art acts as a focal point that ties together your furniture, textiles, and colour palette without overpowering them. In recent years, Islamic calligraphy prints — like this Ayat an-Nur design — have become a particularly popular choice, combining spiritual significance with a genuinely contemporary aesthetic that sits comfortably in modern UK homes.

How to Hang and Style Artwork for a Living Room

1. Measure your wall first: Before ordering, measure the wall space where you plan to hang the print. A good rule of thumb is that artwork should fill around two-thirds to three-quarters of the width of the furniture below it — so above a three-seater sofa, you want a print that feels substantial rather than lost.

2. Find the right height: Hang the centre of the artwork at roughly eye level — typically around 145–150 cm from the floor. This keeps the art connected to the room rather than floating too high on the wall.

3. Choose your framing option: Decide whether you'd like the print framed or unframed. The framed option arrives ready to hang straight away, which is ideal if you want a no-fuss setup. Unframed prints give you the flexibility to choose your own frame to match your existing decor.

4. Consider the lighting: Position a warm light source — a floor lamp or wall light — nearby to bring out the rose gold tones in the calligraphy, especially in the evenings. Natural light from a window works beautifully during the day.

5. Style around the print: Let the print lead your accessory choices. Pick out the dusty blue or blush tones in cushions, throws, or a vase to create a considered, pulled-together look without overcomplicating the space.

Framed vs Unframed: Which Option Is Right for Your Living Room?

Convenience — Framed: arrives ready to hang straight away, no extra shopping needed. Unframed: requires sourcing your own frame, but gives you full control over the finish.

Flexibility — Framed: ideal if you want a complete, polished look quickly. Unframed: perfect if you already have a frame you love or want to match a very specific decor style.

Cost — Framed: slightly higher investment upfront, but saves time and the cost of a separate trip to the shops. Unframed: lower starting price, though frame costs vary widely.

Best for gifting — Framed: makes a more complete, presentation-ready gift — especially lovely for Eid or Ramadan. Unframed: great for recipients who prefer to choose their own frame or already have one in mind.

Wall impact — Framed: the frame adds structure and weight that helps the print command attention on the wall. Unframed: a lighter, more minimal look that suits contemporary or Scandi-influenced interiors.
